hoy.titular: Two days to the final: the Pincha welcomed by their fans in Montevideo

foto.alt: Alexander Medina smiles during an Estudiantes training session.

hoy.resumen: The squad reached their Montevideo hotel through a crowd of fans and train behind closed doors today. Palmeiras are also in Uruguay, with 28 players, for Saturday's final at the Centenario.

siete.texto: After the huge send-off in City Bell, the squad landed at Carrasco and reached the team hotel through hundreds of waiting fans. Thursday's training is behind closed doors and on Friday the press get 15 minutes, plus a press conference.

siete.titulo: Club coaches leave the UNO on Friday at 7am
siete.texto: According to the club, the official coaches leave on Friday 27th at 7am (check-in from 5.30am) and the supporters' groups' coaches at midday, to speed up the border crossing: more than 6,500 people are travelling. A physical ID card or valid passport is required; the Mi Argentina digital ID is not accepted.

siete.titulo: Palmeiras are in Uruguay with 28 players
siete.texto: The Verdão landed in Montevideo with 28 players after a 3-0 defeat by Chapecoense with a reserve side. According to Lance, the squad includes Paulinho, who has been injured since October and remains a doubt. Today they hold their first training session in Montevideo.

siete.titulo: Medina travelled with a 27-man squad, Correa included
siete.texto: The squad list for the final has 27 players and includes Joaquín Correa, who is training with the ball and could get some minutes. The suspended Baltasar Rodríguez and youngsters Pierani, Pereyra and Van der Tuin also travelled.

siete.titulo: Without Baltasar: Fabricio Pérez, Cetré or a back five
siete.texto: According to 0221, Fabricio Pérez is the favourite to replace Baltasar Rodríguez, with Cetré as the alternative; in City Bell Medina also tried Gastón Benedetti in a back five. The line-up will be settled on Friday, in the last training session.

siete.titulo: Verón, just another fan at the Centenario
siete.texto: The president is not travelling with the official party: he is making his own way there and will watch the final from the stands among the fans, as he did at the finals in Santiago del Estero and San Nicolás.
Facundo Mensegues and Brian Froidevaux, two fans from La Plata, reached Montevideo by bicycle after more than 600 kilometres. One of them still has no ticket for the final.
